about: VCF Single Sign-On: Identity Broker deployment modes, supported identity providers and provisioning methods (VCF 9.1 and later).

modes.source: Broadcom TechDocs, VCF 9.1: Identity Broker Detailed Design; Deployment Modes of the Identity Broker
modes.notes: Instance mode runs as a VCF management services component in the management domain of the chosen VCF instance; its size comes from the VCF services runtime, so it adds no separate footprint (Deploy VCF Management Services, VCF 9.1). An embedded broker can later be migrated to instance mode.

embedded.label: Embedded in the management vCenter
embedded.use: Intended for lab or proof-of-concept use, typically within a single VCF instance.

providers.source: Broadcom TechDocs, VCF 9.1: Identity Providers and Protocols Supported for VCF Single Sign-On
providers.notes: One identity provider per identity broker instance. Federated providers use SAML 2.0 or OIDC.

provisioning.source: Broadcom TechDocs, VCF 9.1: Identity Providers and Protocols Supported for VCF Single Sign-On
provisioning.notes: The page lists the methods without mapping them to providers; here SCIM and JIT are offered for federated providers and directory sync for directories.

scim.label: SCIM 2.0 (the identity provider pushes users and groups)

jit.label: Just-in-time (groups created from the SAML assertion or OIDC response at first login)

directory.label: Directory sync (only the users and groups you select, at intervals; passwords are never synced)
